steps.body: Pictures on a page cannot move into a line — so mark them instead: each one gets a tick as its number is said.
steps.narration: Pictures on a page cannot move into a line — so mark them instead: each one gets a tick as its number is said.

widget.prompt: Count 8 printed stars by marking — one counter stands for each tick.

commonCounts.feedback: One star has no tick; an unmarked star is an uncounted star.
A star was ticked twice; each mark must land on a clean star.

widget.missFeedback: Tick each star as its number is said, and count the ticks at the end.
widget.successFeedback: Eight ticks, eight stars — the marks kept counted and uncounted apart.

predict.prompt: Stars printed on a page — how do you keep track while counting?

options.label: Mark each one as it is counted

predict.reveal: A mark does what moving would do: it separates the counted from the uncounted.

cml.actionGoal: Pair each object with exactly one number and trust the last number said for kch count fixed.
invariants: A count pairs objects with number words one to one, and its last word names the whole group — which is why order, spacing, and arrangement can change without changing the answer for kch count fixed.
misconceptions: Skipping or double-counting an object, recounting when nothing changed, or believing a spread-out group holds more.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more object joined the group, what would the last counting word become?

widget.prompt: Tally counts her blocks: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. How many blocks does she have?

options.feedback: Correct — the last number said, 8, tells how many blocks there are in all.
The count stops at 8; saying one more number would count a block that is not there.
That stops one number early — every block gets exactly one number, ending at 8.
That runs two past the count; the last number spoken is the answer, and it was 8.

widget.prompt: The stickers are scattered everywhere. What is the best counting plan?

options.label: Mark or move each one as it is counted
options.feedback: Correct — marking separates the counted from the uncounted, which is what scattered groups make hard.

options.label: Count fast before they move
options.feedback: Speed invites skips and repeats; scattered things need marking, not hurrying.

options.label: Count only the easy ones
options.feedback: Every sticker needs a number, or the final count answers a different question.

options.label: Guess from how big the mess looks
options.feedback: A guess is not a count; the mess can look big with few stickers or small with many.

widget.prompt: Start at 1. Hop forward 3 times by 1. Where do you land?

commonLandings.feedback: 3 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 4.
5 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 3 hops from 1 to land on 4.

widget.missFeedback: Start at 1 and count on 3: you land on 4.
widget.successFeedback: 1 and 3 more is 4 — each hop says the next counting number.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — count all 3 hops, one number per hop, to reach 4.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count stops after exactly 3 hops, on 4.
